reason: The cited evidence does not support the key premises about relative cation diffusivities, interface enrichment, or a transient suboxide mechanism. E1 notes Cr2O3 was absent, contradicting the protective layer premise. E3 shows a Ni-rich bottom layer at 400°C, not a transient suboxide that delays oxygen. E4 shows Al improves oxidation resistance but does not address the specific mechanistic sequence proposed.
premises: Cr and Al have slower outward diffusion than Ni and Mn in HEAs
Slower diffusion of Cr/Al leads to their enrichment at the oxide/alloy interface
This enrichment promotes a continuous, protective Cr2O3/Al2O3 layer
Reducing Cr/Al below a threshold disrupts the protective layer, causing porous scale and higher oxidation rates
A transient Ni/Mn-rich suboxide delays oxygen ingress, aiding selective Cr/Al oxidation
